key_insight: GradAudit uses parameter gradients to spot whether a vision-language model has learned a specific image-text pair during training, rather than just whether each modality appeared separately.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare AI, this could help audit whether patient images and reports may have been used in model training, supporting privacy and provenance checks.
method: Analyzes internal gradient patterns instead of model outputs
Looks for stable, well-aligned gradients on training samples versus noisy gradients on non-training samples
Targets cross-modal image-text associations in VLLMs
evidence_signal: Across medical and general datasets, GradAudit outperformed state-of-the-art baselines in both pretraining and fine-tuning settings, and case studies suggested existing methods underestimate unauthorized data use.
watch_item: Gradient-based auditing may require access to model internals and careful interpretation, so results should not be treated as a complete privacy or copyright verdict.
paper_title: Revealing Training Data Exposure in Vision Language Large Models via Parameter Gradients
